title: Graphical Exploration of the Amplitude Parameter A
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Consider f(x) = A\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{B}(x - C)\right) + D with B = 6 and C = D = 0, so f(x) = A\sin(\pi x / 3). (a) Describe what happens to the graph as A increases through positive values (such as A = 1, 5, 9). (b) What happens to the graph for negative values of A?
finalAnswer: \text{(a) Stretches vertically away from the } x\text{-axis with range } [-A, A]; \quad \text{(b) stretches vertically with amplitude } |A| \text{ and reflects across the } x\text{-axis}

steps.title: Write the Simplified Function and Its Range
steps.explanation: With B = 6 and C = D = 0, the function has period 6, x-intercepts at x = 3k (k in Z), and extreme values +/-|A|.
steps.why: Multiplying sin(pi*x/3) by A scales every y-coordinate by factor A while keeping zeros fixed.

steps.title: Part (a): Effect of Increasing Positive Values of A
steps.mathExpression: A = 1, 5, 9 \implies \text{peaks at } y = A, \; \text{troughs at } y = -A
steps.explanation: As A increases through positive values (1, 5, 9), the graph stretches vertically away from the x-axis: the peaks grow taller and the troughs grow deeper while the x-intercepts remain unchanged.
steps.why: Multiplying a function by A > 1 applies a vertical stretch of factor A.

steps.title: Part (b): Effect of Negative Values of A
steps.explanation: For negative values of A, the graph has amplitude |A| (stretched vertically by |A|) and is reflected across the x-axis, turning peaks into troughs and troughs into peaks.
steps.why: A negative multiplier A = -|A| combines a vertical scaling by |A| with a reflection across the horizontal axis.
